question: Which schema-bound construction and property contracts should HTML, Markdown and plain-text feature mappings share without erasing their format semantics?
trigger: User asks whether another Markdown research/review cycle or an adjacent HTML review is justified, supplying a proposal to derive cross-format tags from the schema.
requirements: Reduce repeated identity, property conversion and child traversal work for current plugin authors while keeping exact inferred schema types.
Preserve CommonMark plus registered-tag grammar, explicit format diagnostics and canonical schema admission; do not promote existing success counts into fidelity or performance guarantees.
Keep persisted schema validity distinct from external interchange policy, semantic HTML, component-rendered presentation and native JSON persistence.
Keep structural HTML, Markdown AST and one-way plain-text jobs honest; exceptions such as URL aliases, captions, list topology, date normalization and secondary roots must remain expressible.
Retain the already-authorized Markdown correctness/proof closure; this review does not authorize downstream cross-format implementation.
evidenceReuse: Reconciled the corrected Markdown prototype and later design/execution record with live source. Read the HTML compiler/authoring types, Markdown types and runtime, plain-text type, representative features, the export menu and prior HTML compiler plans. No broad external-research sweep or new runtime/benchmark claim. Targeted local prior-art reads compared ProseMirror Markdown/DOM construction and Tiptap Markdown spec factories, media attribute allowlists and missing-handler behavior. Local checkout revisions are captured; none is claimed latest.
summary: Pursue a bounded format-mapping authoring design, with HTML as the main comparator. Keep the selected Markdown grammar; another general dialect search has no new decisive requirement. The strongest cut is schema-bound runtime construction and traversal for explicitly declared simple Markdown tags, plus consistent scalar mark values and runtime-owned wrapper children, inside existing format owners. Reject automatic serialization of every installed schema type/property, reuse of custom Plate tags as semantic HTML, and a universal codec/AST/result facade. The supplied proposal overstates parity and wrongly says HTML lacks omitted-property diagnostics; it also mistakes an unassessed ledger scope for no prior HTML authoring work. A full HTML/static audit is not completed by this value review.

reconciliation.question: Which canonical mappings preserve document meaning through Markdown parse/serialize, and where must loss be explicit?
reconciliation.reason: Retain selective registered-tag grammar over the failed HTML-node pairer and the stated proof limits. A 13-document corpus and no grammar throws are not universal fidelity or benchmark closure.

reconciliation.question: Which schema-bound construction and property contracts should HTML, Markdown and plain-text feature mappings share without erasing their format semantics?
reconciliation.reason: Reopen only mapping authoring and completion claims: the report itself leaves failing fixtures and missing browser proof; active mark/attribute repairs are unfinished. Keep grammar selection and format-owned compilation. This cross-format design must not be credited as adoption of the earlier repairs.

reconciliation.question: Which document, projection, schema, format and presentation contracts should own all exports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
reconciliation.reason: Retain direct format-owned conversion, schema/projection authority and separation of semantic export from presentation. Do not reopen later-superseded transfer-report policy in this authoring review.

alternatives: Keep the selected CommonMark plus registered-tag parser and finish current repairs: retain. There is no new grammar requirement or contradictory recognizer evidence that pays for another broad GitHub search.

Keep all mapping construction handwritten: loses for simple bound tags and scalar marks, where repeated schema identity, attributes and recursive child handling are owned by the compiler already. Keep callbacks for real format-specific transforms.

Proposed explicit declaration such as defineFormats({ markdown: { tag: type, properties: ["width"] } }): pursue as a design candidate. Existing Markdown compiler can own node construction, declared attribute conversion and schema-directed child traversal; exact syntax and whether an explicit property selection or another bounded policy wins remain open.

Derive mark/element call shapes from the schema binding and remove redundant role declarations; compare a shared format-neutral property-value contract privately. This may delete more author work than a helper returning the same verbose mapping, without introducing another plugin or namespace.

Automatically convert every schema type/property to a tag and reuse those tags as HTML: reject. Schema identity/validation does not specify a useful HTML representation, raw attributes versus properties, metadata inclusion, URL aliases, captions, generated IDs or atom text. The existing ElementId metadata/copy law and media URL/caption consumers are concrete counterexamples.

Route all Markdown tags and raw HTML through the HTML parser: do not adopt wholesale. It would couple a pure syntax path to DOM semantics and conflict with the retained registered-tag dialect; consider a targeted adapter only for a named raw-HTML user job.

Merge HTML, Markdown, plain text, DOCX and static rendering into one codec or public AST/result: reject. Plain-text projection, semantic interchange, visual rendering and package artifacts have different directions, syntax and lifecycle. Reuse only proven private mechanics at Plate; Plite retains schema/model law.

Prior art supports explicit reuse rather than schema-wide automatic exposure: ProseMirror parser state constructs nodes at close; Tiptap exposes opt-in Pandoc block/atom Markdown spec factories and Audio supplies allowedAttributes. These are analogues, not the same registered-tag grammar or proof that Plate is the best editor. Tiptap returns an empty string for an unknown renderer; ProseMirror throws by default. Preserve Plate structured refusals instead of copying either failure contract.

Next owner: $task design plan format-mappings: simplify schema-bound HTML and Markdown authoring, remove repeated construction and traversal, and preserve explicit format semantics. Begin by proving representative tag/property cases and the strongest counterexamples before choosing a generic declaration.
proofLimits: Read-only value assessment of three authoring contracts and representative consumers, not an exhaustive conversion/HTML/static audit. No fresh full tests, browser, native artifact, benchmark or claim to be best among editors. Markdown execution proof remains partial/stale with existing fixture, browser and durable benchmark follow-up. Active working-tree repairs can change captured mapping signatures; this record does not adopt or verify their unfinished implementation. Schema-derived tag DX/runtime wins are design candidates, not measured production improvements. Upstream evidence is source inspection only at recorded local commits; no competitor performance or compatibility experiments were run.
